title: TNFR-Python-Engine: Resonant Fractal Nature Theory Implementation
description:
TNFR-Python-Engine is a Python research framework for organized mathematical objects under declared nodal laws. It investigates their identity, dynamics, interactions and emergent properties while retaining the constituent and boundary information needed to predict response. The relation dEPI/dt = nu_f DeltaNFR describes the unforced continuous form row; pressure, phase, capacity, support, clock, inputs and event laws require explicit premises.

Version 0.0.4 treats the thirteen registered structural operators and their grammar as the constitutive mechanisms under study: continuous, native relational and collective descriptions must be grounded in actual operator execution or a proved realization. It integrates operator-level results on Resonance and Contraction maintenance with ordered return, retained synthesis and response sufficiency, coupling between connected organizations, finite-duration Emission, native Mutation occurrence and abstention, operator growth and recursive post-birth participation, with shared kernels, atomic stages and tests. Admission, preservation of a reference region and actual occurrence remain distinct obligations; supplied words are interventions, not autonomous selection.

Four foundation prerequisites (operator causality, state and observation, organizational identity and research selection) are resolved within reviewed mathematical scopes with independent reviews, and a checked readiness gate keeps physical mapping blocked until a final review. The research program is modular, with one current question, canonical chapters and a theory-to-execution map. Under a new retention policy the repository keeps the material that serves active research; secondary campaign evidence, a consumed attempt, archived applications and historical captures were retired with permalinks to their recovery commit. Each release also ships a lightweight development bundle with verified retrieval of omitted evidence.

Exact identities, conditional mathematical proofs, finite computational evidence, diagnostic policies and open hypotheses retain distinct status. These results do not constitute empirical validation, derive autonomous occurrence or select a unique fundamental law. The objective is to investigate the scope of TNFR without prescribing the outcome.

See the 0.0.4 release, versioned source, Python package, theory catalog and current documentation.
